verdict.label: STEP ASIDE — Weekend Reflection: A Regime Break, Then Iran Strikes; CPI June 10 Is the Binary
verdict.rationale_short: Markets are closed (Saturday). No new equity prints since Friday's break, so this is a reflection on a week that ended in the worst regime state of the series — and a weekend that made it worse. Friday's hot 172K NFP (vs 85K consensus) broke the framework: SPX -2.64% to 7,383.74 (below the 7,460 floor), VIX +34% to ~20.9 (above 18), the 30Y at 5.007%, NVDA stopped out at $215, and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index posting its worst session since March 2020. Crypto cratered alongside — BTC fell as low as ~$59,227, ETH broke below $1,900, ~$390B in market value erased. Then over the weekend the US and Iran exchanged strikes near the Strait of Hormuz, straining the ceasefire further. STEP ASIDE holds at medium — not bearish — only because the May CPI on June 10 is an unresolved binary that could either confirm the higher-for-longer break or relieve it; one hot labor print plus a weekend escalation is not yet a trend. Capital preservation, not bottom-fishing.

bear_case: A reflection on a closed Saturday is where to be honest that this is no longer a dip — it is a regime change pending one confirmation. Friday broke three indicators at once (VIX above 18, the S&P below its 7,460 floor, the 30Y at 5.0%+), the semis had their worst day since March 2020, crypto lost ~$390B, and over the weekend the US and Iran traded strikes near the world's most important oil chokepoint. The single thread holding the verdict at STEP ASIDE rather than bearish is that May CPI on June 10 has not printed — and if it comes in hot (headline toward 4.2% with sticky core), the higher-for-longer break is confirmed, the Warsh FOMC on June 16-17 becomes a live hike, and Friday's lows will not hold. The weekend Iran escalation removes the one offsetting hope (that falling oil would ease inflation): with strikes near Hormuz, the energy tail is widening again. Invalidation level: a hot CPI June 10 with the 30Y closing above 5.05% converts STEP ASIDE to bearish and targets SPX 7,200-7,250; only a cool CPI with VIX back below 18 and the 30Y below 5.0% restores a HOLD.
